Twelve men walked on the [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon") during six [Moon landings](/wiki/Moon_landing "Moon landing") of the [Apollo program](/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program") between July 1969 and December 1972. All landed on the surface only once, and five missions consisted of two or more surface [extravehicular activities (EVAs)](/wiki/Extravehicular_activity "Extravehicular activity"). Four of them are alive as of February 2026 with an average age of 92.9
years. Most astronauts at that time came from the military services and were considered to be on active duty during their NASA service. The few exceptions were considered civilian NASA astronauts, regardless of any prior military service.

On the last of their three Apollo 17 EVAs, [Harrison Schmitt](/wiki/Harrison_Schmitt "Harrison Schmitt") stepped out of the [Apollo Lunar Module](/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module "Apollo Lunar Module") onto the surface of the Moon after [Gene Cernan](/wiki/Gene_Cernan "Gene Cernan"), and is therefore the 12th and most recent person to have stepped out onto the Moon. When they re-entered the Lunar Module Cernan stepped in last, and is therefore the last person to have walked on the Moon.

[Alan Shepard](/wiki/Alan_Shepard "Alan Shepard") was the oldest person to walk on the Moon, at age 47 years and 80 days. [Charles Duke](/wiki/Charles_Duke "Charles Duke") was the youngest, at age 36 years and 201 days.

[Jim Lovell](/wiki/Jim_Lovell "Jim Lovell") and [Fred Haise](/wiki/Fred_Haise "Fred Haise") were scheduled to walk on the Moon during the [Apollo 13](/wiki/Apollo_13 "Apollo 13") mission, but the lunar landing was aborted following an explosion in the spacecraft [service module](/wiki/Service_module "Service module") en route to the Moon. fanoutqa_006535.x:
Chichen Itza :: Tourism :: part 02 :: chunk_0030
Chichen Itza, a UNESCO [World Heritage Site](/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site"), is the second-most visited of Mexico's archeological sites.[[102]](#cite_note-108) The archeological site draws many visitors from the popular tourist resorts in [Cancún](/wiki/Canc%C3%BAn "Cancún"), who make a day trip on tour buses.

In 2007, Chichen Itza's Temple of Kukulcán (El Castillo) was named one of the [New Seven Wonders of the World](/wiki/New_Seven_Wonders_of_the_World "New Seven Wonders of the World") after a worldwide vote.[[103]](#cite_note-Hindustan_times-109) Despite the fact that the vote was sponsored by a commercial enterprise, and that its methodology was criticized, the vote was embraced by government and tourism officials in Mexico who projected that as a result of the publicity the number of tourists to Chichén would double by 2012.[[nb 7]](#cite_note-110)[[104]](#cite_note-111) The ensuing publicity re-ignited debate in Mexico over the ownership of the site, which culminated on 29 March 2010 when the state of Yucatán purchased the land upon which the most recognized monuments rest from owner Hans Juergen Thies Barbachano.[[105]](#cite_note-112)

INAH, which manages the site, has closed a number of monuments to public access. While visitors can walk around them, they can no longer climb them or go inside their chambers. Climbing access to El Castillo was closed after an American woman fell to her death in 2006.[[62]](#cite_note-DiarioYucatan3Mar06-66)

Mexico is a [federal republic](/wiki/Federal_republic "Federal republic") with a [presidential system of government](/wiki/President_of_Mexico "President of Mexico"), characterized by a democratic framework and the separation of powers into three branches: [executive](/wiki/Executive_(government) "Executive (government)"), legislative, and judicial. The federal legislature consists of the [bicameral](/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") [Congress of the Union](/wiki/Congress_of_the_Union "Congress of the Union"), comprising the [Chamber of Deputies](/wiki/Chamber_of_Deputies_(Mexico) "Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)"), which represents the population, and the [Senate](/wiki/Senate_of_the_Republic_(Mexico) "Senate of the Republic (Mexico)"), which provides equal representation for each state. The Constitution establishes three levels of government: the federal Union, the state governments, and the municipal governments. Mexico's federal structure grants autonomy to its 32 states, and its political system is deeply influenced by indigenous traditions and [European Enlightenment](/wiki/European_Enlightenment "European Enlightenment") ideals.

Mexico is a [newly industrialized](/wiki/Newly_industrialized_country "Newly industrialized country") and [developing country](/wiki/Developing_country "Developing country"),[[14]](#cite_note-Globalization2-17) with the world's [15th-largest economy by nominal GDP](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of countries by GDP (nominal)") and the [13th-largest by purchasing power parity (PPP)](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(PPP) "List of countries by GDP (PPP)"). Yellen is married to [George Akerlof](/wiki/George_Akerlof "George Akerlof"), an economist who is a university professor at the [McCourt School of Public Policy](/wiki/McCourt_School_of_Public_Policy "McCourt School of Public Policy") at [Georgetown University](/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") and Koshland Professor of Economics Emeritus at the [University of California, Berkeley](/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"), as well as a 2001 [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") laureate.[[22]](#cite_note-NobelPrize-22)[[246]](#cite_note-246) The couple met in the fall of 1977, became engaged by that December, and married in June 1978, less than a year after meeting.[[247]](#cite_note-Foroohar,_Time-247)[[21]](#cite_note-FedLove,_Reuters-21)

Their son, Robert Akerlof (born 1981), is a fellow economist. He received a bachelor's *summa cum laude* in economics and mathematics from Yale University in 2003 and earned his Ph.D. in economics from Harvard University in 2009, where he was a Presidential Scholar. After two years as a postdoc at [MIT](/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology"), and 14 years at the [University of Warwick](/wiki/University_of_Warwick "University of Warwick") as an assistant and associate professor of economics, in 2024, he became a full professor of economics at the [UNSW Business School](/wiki/UNSW_Business_School "UNSW Business School") in Sydney.[[248]](#cite_note-R.AkerlofCV2-248)

Yellen and George Akerlof have often collaborated on research, including topics such as poverty, unemployment and a paper on the costs of out-of-wedlock childbearing. A third entry in the MCU Spider-Man franchise began development shortly after Sony and Marvel's contract was effective.[[106]](#cite_note-DisneySonySpidey3-107) Watts continued his duties as director,[[130]](#cite_note-Foxx-131) while McKenna and Sommers returned to write the screenplay of what would become *Spider-Man: No Way Home*.[[131]](#cite_note-WattsDeadlineAug2019-132) The writers conceived a [multiverse](/wiki/Multiverse_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Multiverse (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") story from an idea inspired by the fantasy drama *[It's a Wonderful Life](/wiki/It%27s_a_Wonderful_Life "It's a Wonderful Life")* (1946), wherein Peter convinces [Dr. Stephen Strange](/wiki/Stephen_Strange_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Stephen Strange (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") ([Benedict Cumberbatch](/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch")) to reverse the events leading to the exposure of his identity as Spider-Man with a [spell](/wiki/Incantation "Incantation").[[132]](#cite_note-McKennaSommers2-133) The film connects Sony's Spider-Man universes to the MCU and features several of the associated characters, including Maguire and Garfield's Spider-Men.[[132]](#cite_note-McKennaSommers2-133)[[133]](#cite_note-134)[[134]](#cite_note-NWHPastVillains-135) *No Way Home*'s production lasted from October 2020 to March 2021,[[135]](#cite_note-136) and the film debuted in theaters in December 2021.[[136]](#cite_note-137) By the end of the global rollout, it became the [highest-grossing film of 2021](/wiki/2021_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2021 in film") with a box office take of $1.910 billion.[[137]](#cite_note-138)[[i]](#cite_note-reissue-139)

Map showing the member states of the European Union (clickable)

Through successive [enlargements](/wiki/Enlargement_of_the_European_Union "Enlargement of the European Union"), the EU and its predecessors have grown from the [six founding states](/wiki/Inner_Six "Inner Six") of the EEC to 27 members. Countries accede to the union by becoming a party to the founding [treaties](/wiki/Treaties_of_the_European_Union "Treaties of the European Union"), thereby subjecting themselves to the privileges and obligations of EU membership. This entails a partial delegation of sovereignty to the institutions in return for representation within those institutions, a practice often referred to as "pooling of sovereignty".[[72]](#cite_note-85)[[73]](#cite_note-86) In some policies, there are several member states that ally with strategic partners within the union. Examples of such alliances include the [Baltic Assembly](/wiki/Baltic_Assembly "Baltic Assembly"), the [Benelux Union](/wiki/Benelux_Union "Benelux Union"), the [Bucharest Nine](/wiki/Bucharest_Nine "Bucharest Nine"), the [Craiova Group](/wiki/Craiova_Group "Craiova Group"), the [EU Med Group](/wiki/EU_Med_Group "EU Med Group"), the [Lublin Triangle](/wiki/Lublin_Triangle "Lublin Triangle"), the [New Hanseatic League](/wiki/New_Hanseatic_League "New Hanseatic League"), the [Three Seas Initiative](/wiki/Three_Seas_Initiative "Three Seas Initiative"), the [Visegrád Group](/wiki/Visegr%C3%A1d_Group "Visegrád Group"), and the [Weimar Triangle](/wiki/Weimar_Triangle "Weimar Triangle").

Charles served in the [Royal Air Force](/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force") (RAF) and the [Royal Navy](/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") during the 1970s. His military training began in 1969, in his second year at Cambridge, when he joined the [Cambridge University Air Squadron](/wiki/Cambridge_University_Air_Squadron "Cambridge University Air Squadron") and learned to fly the [Chipmunk](/wiki/De_Havilland_Canada_DHC-1_Chipmunk "De Havilland Canada DHC-1 Chipmunk").[[41]](#cite_note-48)[[42]](#cite_note-49) He was presented with his [RAF wings](/wiki/Aircrew_brevet "Aircrew brevet") in August 1971.[[43]](#cite_note-50)

[![Three county-class destroyers sailing in the English Channel](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/County_class%2C_1970_%28IWM%29.jpg/250px-County_class%2C_1970_%28IWM%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:County_class,_1970_(IWM).jpg)

Charles was serving aboard *Norfolk* at this time.

After the [passing-out](/wiki/Passing_out_(military) "Passing out (military)") parade that September, Charles embarked on a naval career and undertook a six-week course at the [Royal Naval College, Dartmouth](/wiki/Royal_Naval_College,_Dartmouth "Royal Naval College, Dartmouth"). He subsequently served from 1971 to 1972 on the guided-missile destroyer [HMS *Norfolk*](/wiki/HMS_Norfolk_(D21) "HMS Norfolk (D21)"), and on the frigates [HMS *Minerva*](/wiki/HMS_Minerva_(F45) "HMS Minerva (F45)") from 1972 to 1973 and [HMS *Jupiter*](/wiki/HMS_Jupiter_(F60) "HMS Jupiter (F60)") in 1974. In 2017, Gerwig made her solo directorial debut (after having co-directed *Nights and Weekends*) with the coming-of-age comedy-drama film *[Lady Bird](/wiki/Lady_Bird_(film) "Lady Bird (film)")*, which she also wrote.[[52]](#cite_note-52) It starred [Saoirse Ronan](/wiki/Saoirse_Ronan "Saoirse Ronan") in the title role.[[53]](#cite_note-53) *Lady Bird* premiered at the [Telluride Film Festival](/wiki/Telluride_Film_Festival "Telluride Film Festival") and was theatrically released in November 2017. The film grossed over $78 million against its $10 million budget worldwide. *Lady Bird* received critical acclaim, with reviewers particularly lauding Gerwig's screenplay and direction.[[54]](#cite_note-54)[[55]](#cite_note-55) The film was chosen by the [National Board of Review](/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review"), the [American Film Institute](/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute"), and *[Time](/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* magazine as one of the top ten films of 2017.[[56]](#cite_note-56)[[57]](#cite_note-NBR-57)[[58]](#cite_note-58) According to the review-aggregation website [Rotten Tomatoes](/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), it was given 196 positive reviews in a row, making it the record-holder for the most "fresh" reviews,[[59]](#cite_note-59) until the first "rotten" one arrived in December 2017.[[60]](#cite_note-60) As of 2019, it had a 99% rating on the aforementioned website.[[61]](#cite_note-61)
